ContextMenu_KCS_ASH_6: All crushed in the same spot; the bottom is worn shiny there.
ContextMenu_KCS_ASH_7: Only one butt, but the ash is deep. The rest were tipped out.

ContextMenu_KCS_EMBC_1: Cold. There was still some warmth in it a moment ago.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMBC_2: Burned down to the filter and went out on its own. Nobody came back.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMBC_3: Now it is no different from the few hundred other butts on the ground.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMBC_4: The ash has collapsed. One breath of wind and it is gone.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMBC_5: You missed it by the length of one cigarette.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_1: Only this one in the ashtray. He finished it and left without waiting for it to go out.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_10: Half of it, then out. He heard something.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_11: There's a scorch on the rim where it burned itself. It was set down wrong.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_12: Smoked until it was too hot to hold. This one wasn't in a hurry.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_13: A matchstick beside it, snapped in two. The first strike didn't take.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_14: Not stubbed out - left there to finish on its own. Somebody meant to come back.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_15: A receipt pinned under the tray, one corner gone yellow with smoke.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_16: The length of one cigarette. He stood here for the length of one cigarette.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_2: The filter is chewed flat. He was thinking about something else while he smoked.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_3: A quarter of it left. Somebody called his name.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_4: Stubbed against the bottom of the tray, then let go halfway.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_5: Lipstick on the filter. She left before he did.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_6: The ash is straight, not one break in it. Nobody touched this one from end to end.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_7: Laid down square with the rim of the tray. This one's hands don't shake.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_8: The filter is still damp. Put down less than five minutes ago.
ContextMenu_KCS_EMB_9: The tray is wiped clean apart from this. Somebody was still keeping order.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AmericanBlend: Four old brands' family secrets, safe on paper now.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AromaticBooklet: The last page is an order form. Nobody ships anymore.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AshClay: Some kid's craft-class project. Dad said it was beautiful.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AshGlass: Bar-grade glass ashtray. The missing chip has a story of its own.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AshPorcelain: Diner porcelain. It has seen more late nights than you.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AshSteel: Stamped steel, factory issue. Also cracks walnuts.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AshenCommunionMs: The page edges are scorched. Ritual or accident, no one can say.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AshtrayBeanbag: Sits on a sofa arm and does not tip. That was the entire pitch.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AshtrayMug: An old mug with the handle still on. Nobody drinks from it now.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AshtrayPromoGlass: Free with a carton in 1988. The logo is on the bottom, upside down.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AshtraySodaCan: A cut-open can. Works. Cuts you if you are careless.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AshtrayStanding: Brass column, hotel lobby stock. Heavy on purpose so it stays put.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_AshtrayTinCan: A tin can with the label soaked off. It holds ash. That is the whole review.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_Assorted: What's inside depends on what was at hand when somebody filled it.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_B_AshenCommunion: The recipe was never written down, which is why it is still argued about.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_B_AshfordNo7: Nobody knows how recipes one through six ended up. Seven worked.

ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_B_LastLight: There is no carton of these. There was never going to be.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_B_Midnight100s: The long ones, for people who don't sleep. You weren't sleeping anyway.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_B_OldMillReds: The mill is gone; the recipe isn't. Old-fashioned harsh, old-fashioned steady.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_B_Pinecrest: Smells like a pine forest. Smokes like a pine forest on fire.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_B_Riverbend: The pride of Riverbend. Riverbend has two streets.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_Beyond: It shouldn't be here. Then again, neither should you.

ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_Celestial: On the back of the pack: before dawn, learn to see in the dark.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_Chew: Great-grandfather chewed this. That's also when the teeth went.

ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_DisposableFreight: Bought by the box for a loading dock, where it lived.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_DisposableGas2Go: The chain printed these by the crate and sold two stations.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_DisposableGreen: Neon green so it turns up again. It usually does not.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_DisposableOrange: Hunting orange, so it is visible to everything except deer.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_DisposablePink: Borrowed once by everybody, returned once by nobody.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_Dossier: Four manuscripts bound as one. Beyond the county line, is anyone still smoking?
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_Fable: Tiny print on the paper: every one of these is an unfinished story.

ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_GenericButt: Butts off the ground carry no brand. Only history.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_GrowingManual: A margin note on page 37: tobacco seedlings are like people - harvest too early and you ruin them.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_H_AshenCommunion: The ashen communion. The church never approved the rite - never stopped it either.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_H_BeyondCounty: Rolled past the county line. The tobacco crossed before the paperwork did.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_H_NightWatch: Rolled by the ones who kept watch. Afterwards, the dark minds its manners.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_H_OldPhysician: The old doctor's blend: cures nothing, but the pain starts keeping office hours.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_H_SilentHunt: A recipe hunters passed only to hunters: quiet, steady hands, no questions.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_KitchenMatchbox: Two hundred fifty, blue tips, for the whole household. Strike on the side.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_LastLight: Kept for the last hours. Before the lights go out, something ought to stay lit.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_Lighter: Lost three times, came back twice. That already counts as loyalty.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_LighterFluidLarge: Twelve ounces. Keep it away from the thing you are lighting.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_LighterFluidSmall: Four ounces. Refills a flip-top a dozen times if you don't spill.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookAlbum: Holds thirteen. Carry it or shelve it - either way it pays.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookBowling: Twenty matches. Shoe rental, seventy-five cents, printed before the sign changed.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookCaseComplet: Thirteen of thirteen. The Committee counted twice and finally stopped counting.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookCaseEmpty: Thirteen slots, twelve books in the county. Do the arithmetic.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookCaseFilled: Filling up. The empty slot is not an accident.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookCheckpoint: Twenty matches. The instructions on the back stop making sense halfway down.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookDrake: Twenty matches, from the only hotel in the county with a doorman.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookFossoil: Twenty matches. Free with a fill-up, back when that came with a conversation.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookGas2Go: Twenty matches. The only thing that chain made and people kept.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookPileOCrepe: Twenty matches. They printed five thousand and served about nine hundred people.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookPoolHall: Twenty matches. Plain black, two words, no address.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookPrison: Twenty matches. A serial number where the phone number goes.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookSeahorse: Twenty matches, from a motel that rented by the week.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookSpiffos: Twenty matches. The mascot is looking slightly to your left.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookTheatre: Twenty matches. Thirty years of booth smoke made the screen two whites.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookWarehouse: Twenty matches. Plain kraft, nothing printed, nothing to advertise.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MatchbookZippee: Twenty matches. Bright green means a drawer; grey means it was carried.

ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_Memo: The county seal is still crisp. The hand that stamped it is gone.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_MentholGuide: Menthol is a matter of measure: too little is soulless, too much bites.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_NightShift: For everyone on night shift: there is one cigarette left between you and dawn.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_NightWatchMs: Hurried handwriting, as if racing the sunrise.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_NoveltyCatfish: Gas-station rack. The whiskers snap off first, usually in a pocket.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_NoveltyGhoul: Glows in the dark, badly. Sold better after the news started.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_NoveltyMuscleCar: A car nobody in this county could afford, on a lighter anybody could.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_NoveltyPinup: The print wears off the front first. It always did.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_NoveltyRevolver: Shaped like a gun, lights like a lighter. Do not wave it at anyone.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_OldPhysicianMs: Prescription-style script; the signature can never be verified now.

ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_PremiumNotes: Every line between these lines smells of money.

ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_RollingPrimer: The cover is dog-eared. Its last owner clearly learned while rolling.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_SilentHuntMs: A hunter's hand: every stroke steady, like aiming.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_Spiffo: Spiffo smiles at you. Spiffo always smiles at you.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_SpiffoAshtray: Stubbing one out on the mascot's face is oddly therapeutic.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_SpiffoLighter: The million-light guarantee is printed on the bottom. Very small.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_StormproofMatches: These burn in the rain. That is the only thing they are better at.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_WishbonePack: A whole pack wishing in the same direction.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoAce: The ace is off-centre by a hair, and always was.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoBlack: Plain, cheap, and it outsold every fancy one four to one.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoBourbon: The distillery it advertises closed in 1991.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoBrass: Unlacquered: it darkens wherever your thumb goes.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoCamo: Useless at hiding a lighter. It was never hiding the lighter.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoChrome: Shows every fingerprint. People polished it anyway.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoDerby: The horse's back is worn smooth. That's the thumb.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoFlag: In a dark bar, the easiest one on the table to find again.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoMermaid: From a seafood place four hundred miles from any sea.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoMiner: A retirement gift, handed out eleven months early.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoMoon: The moon phases run backwards. The corrected batch sold worse.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoRackEmpty: Fourteen slots and a velvet pedestal. All of them empty.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoRackFew: A start. The pedestal on top is still waiting.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoRackFull: Fourteen of fourteen. The pedestal is a separate question.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoRackHonor: The pedestal is occupied. The veterans know whose it is.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoRackMost: Nearly there. You already know which one is missing.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoRiverBelle: The boat stopped running sixteen years before this shipped.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoRoadHawk: Faded on one side only. That side faced the sun.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoSnake: Everyone calls it ugly. It sold out every year.
ContextMenu_KCS_FLV_ZeddoVeteran: Two engravings, twenty-five years apart. Both hand-cut.
ContextMenu_KCS_FireChoiceUnavailable: That fire source is no longer available.
ContextMenu_KCS_HWHint_KCS_SpiffosAlibiA: They say a room goes quiet when it is set down nearby.
ContextMenu_KCS_HWHint_KCS_SpiffosAlibiL: They say it was there that night.
ContextMenu_KCS_HWHint_KCS_ZeddoVeteran: The one that was engraved twice.
ContextMenu_KCS_HWStory_KCS_SpiffosAlibi: Nobody came for it the day the restaurant closed, so it stayed where it was. The glass is absurdly thick, and there is a burn ring underneath that will not come off. Set it down and you find yourself talking more quietly.
A heavy brass promotional lighter whose fuel gauge never moves. Taken in for repair three times, pronounced fine three times. It weighs more than a lighter ought to, and the hand remembers the shape.
ContextMenu_KCS_HWStory_KCS_ZeddoVeteran: The front reads "Hue 1968", cut at his own asking; the back reads "For Little Danny 1993", cut twenty-five years later in a different hand and a different depth. Of the twenty-five years between them there is no record. Carried, the hand does not shake -- that is how he put it, and nobody who heard it asked further.

ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_Bowling: League nights were Tuesday and Thursday and the whole building smelled of lane oil and fryer grease. The matchbook advertises shoe rental at seventy-five cents, a price that had been crossed out and rewritten twice by hand on the sign inside.
ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_Checkpoint: Printed in a hurry in the second week, when an office decided the men standing in the road needed something to hand people. The back carries a numbered list of instructions. Read it now and you can see the exact line where the writing stops believing itself.
ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_Drake: The only hotel in the county with a doorman, and he was also the bellhop and, after nine, the bartender. The matchbook is heavier stock than the others. That was the whole idea.
ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_Fossoil: Free with a fill-up, back when a fill-up came with a conversation. The new owner worked out in 1991 that they cost eleven cents a book and sold no extra gasoline, and he was right about both. The pumps have been quiet ever since.
ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_Gas2Go: The chain that put a store on four corners of the same intersection and then wondered why three of them lost money. The matchbook is the only thing they ever made that people kept. It says OPEN 24 HOURS, which stopped being true in the second week.
ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_PileOCrepe: A pancake house that was busiest at two in the morning, which tells you most of what you need to know about it. The matchbook has a phone number for a location that closed in 1988; they never reprinted, and the staff got used to saying so.
ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_PoolHall: No sign outside; the address travelled by word of mouth and never needed printing. The matchbook is plain black with two words on it. If you have to ask which two, the place was not for you.
ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_Prison: Visitor centre issue, one book per visit, matches counted out on the way in and counted again on the way out. The cover carries no name and no address. Whoever kept this one kept it for a reason that had nothing to do with smoking.
ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_Seahorse: A motel with an empty pool and a vacancy sign that still worked. Rooms went by the week to people between things. On the nightstand: a Bible with an uncracked spine, an ashtray with none.
ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_Spiffos: Handed out by the fistful at the register, which is why a house always held more of them than the household remembered taking. The mascot on the cover looks slightly to the left of whoever holds it. Children found this funny; adults, after a while, stopped mentioning it.
ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_Theatre: One screen, one show a night, and a marquee that lost letters faster than the manager could replace them. For most of 1993 it read THE FUGI IVE. Nobody complained, and a few people preferred it.
ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_Warehouse: Plain kraft, no printing at all, bought by the case for places that needed matches and had nothing to advertise. Loading docks, back offices, church halls. The most common book in the county, and the last one to make it onto a collector's list.
ContextMenu_KCS_MBStory_Zippee: A convenience store that sold more lottery tickets than food. The green on the cover fades to grey inside a year in a shirt pocket, so the colour dates the book better than the print does: bright means a drawer, grey means every day.
ContextMenu_KCS_MSHint_KCS_AshenCommunio: Nobody admits to having written it.
ContextMenu_KCS_MSHint_KCS_BeyondCountyD: Bound up, this sort of thing is not called a manuscript. It is called a file.
ContextMenu_KCS_MSHint_KCS_NightWatchMan: Two half-pages copied into one. Whose handwriting, nobody knows.
ContextMenu_KCS_MSHint_KCS_OldPhysicianM: Left by a physician. The purpose is in question.
ContextMenu_KCS_MSHint_KCS_SilentHuntMan: Written for people who would rather not be heard.
ContextMenu_KCS_MSStory_KCS_AshenCommuni: Assembled out of four fragments, four hands, four people. None of them signed. Whoever copied it added at the end: if you copy it too, do not sign.
ContextMenu_KCS_MSStory_KCS_BeyondCounty: What lies past the county line, set down item by item, sorted, numbered. The numbering stops at 47 and the pages after it are blank. It does not say why it stops, and it does not say what 47 was.
ContextMenu_KCS_MSStory_KCS_NightWatchMa: The night shift blended their own: the process on one sheet, the ratios on another, never kept together. That way, he said, half of it is worth nothing to anybody. Somebody did take half of it, later.
ContextMenu_KCS_MSStory_KCS_OldPhysician: Written by a retired county-hospital doctor. The first paragraph is a defence of himself: this is not medicine, only something certain patients needed in his view. The recipe comes after. In the last few lines the hand is visibly unsteady.
ContextMenu_KCS_MSStory_KCS_SilentHuntMa: There is nothing remarkable in the recipe itself; what is remarkable is the slow step it insists on. Hurry it and the taste scatters. The hunter who copied it wrote in the margin: it belongs to whoever can wait.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_AfterFight_desc: Twenty-five lit while the hands were still shaking.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_AllBrands_desc: Every commercial brand tasted at least once.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_ButtPile_desc: Twenty butts on one square. You have used that ground up.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_Cadger_desc: Fifty smokes lit from nearby stoves, fireplaces, barbecues or campfires.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_Collector_desc: Thirteen matchbooks gathered from thirteen corners of the county.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_CoughFuture_desc: A hundred coughs, all of them earned. Each one was free advertising.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_Coupons_desc: Find 10 brand mileage coupons inside packs.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_DannyHome_desc: The veteran's Zeddo found its way back to someone who understands.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_EmptyShelf_desc: Ten empty packs of different brands, carried at once. You keep them because they keep you.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_FullSet_desc: All three Alibi pieces, one smoke, witnessed.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_HiddenHint: Not yet the moment to say it out loud.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_Hundred_desc: One hundred finished. The county knows your brand of quiet.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_KeyringMatch_desc: Lit a cigarette with the permanent match.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_Lamplighter_desc: Every one of the fourteen Zeddo finishes has passed through your hands.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_LastMatch_desc: One left in the box, and it caught.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_MorningStreak_desc: Ten days running, the first one after waking.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_NeverReturns_desc: Thirty lights cadged with nothing of your own. Some people are just like that.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_RainLight_desc: Lit in the rain with a stormproof match.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_SmokyRoom_desc: Five different ashtrays set out in one room.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_Thousand_desc: One thousand finished. A legend with yellow fingers.
ContextMenu_KCS_MS_Wishbone_desc: You found the flipped one, and you smoked it.

ContextMenu_KCS_RackHonorLocked: The pedestal waits until all fourteen shine

ContextMenu_KCS_RollScavenged: Roll a scavenged cigarette (%1 butts + 1 paper)
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_AshenCommunion: Ritual smokes of a nameless congregation; no one knows where the chapel is, only that the ash must be kept in a tin. When the flame rises, fear is collected as an offering, and the smoker is responsible only for breathing. On the paper, a faded line: do not give thanks.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_AshfordNo7: The recipe was rewritten six times; the seventh was right. Factory folk say the first six formula sheets were burned and the ash buried under the foundations - never confirmed, never dug up. The 7 doesn't mean a seventh flavour. It means the seventh time, nobody gave up.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_BeyondCounty: A footnote on the recipe reads: not recorded in any county annals. The leaf has no traceable field, the rolling plant no address, even the tax stamp is blank. Afterwards the boundary stones seem closer - and that feeling outlasts the taste.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_BeyondScreen: It belongs to no county and no save file. The wrapper is standard missing-texture pink-and-purple check, yet it is real to the touch. Rise high enough and the smoke passes through a pane of invisible glass - someone on the other side is watching you through a screen, and every cigarette you smoke, you smoke for the both of you.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_BlackOakReserve: The leaf ages eighteen months in oak barrels retired from a bourbon distillery. A little sweetness stays behind, as if someone rounded the day off for you. Specific medicine for rotten days - county folk keep it for weddings and funerals alike, for the same reason.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_BluegrassSelect: The billboard at the Route 57 junction shows a meadow bent flat by wind, with one line of copy: like a Sunday. Every spring the company sponsors the high-school baseball season; the prize is a tin with the team crest. People who buy it say it smokes like a day off. People who don't say that's because they never had one.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_Buckhorn: On the shelf the first day of hunting season, gone the last - eleven weeks a year. Two drags and your legs stop aching; the stand hunters call it their second pair of boots. The deer calendar is printed on the back, and old hunters nail the empty packs to the cabin wall like tree rings.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_Celestial: Left behind by the second coauthor. Sun, Terra and Luna take turns on the face of the box, watching the dark for you - whenever you rest, one of them is awake. Late in the pack the box changes its name, like a change of watch. It doesn't hurry you through the night. It just keeps you company.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_CoalCreek: Hand-rolled in the old Coal Creek workshop, forty a day, thick as a mine at night. Courage in stick form, one counts as three - townsmen smoke half before going down, tuck the other half in the hatband, and finish it topside. Four generations in, the shop sign has never been repainted.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_Coauthored: Two packs bound into one volume at the same desk; the binding thread is a wisp of smoke that never dispersed. No order of signatures - inside the flyleaf it says: who wrote first doesn't matter, what matters is that neither stopped. Whoever smokes the last one signs the final page for them both.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_CumberlandKings: Three generations of Cumberland coal miners smoked this brand, harsh enough to sit on an old back injury. The crown on the pack is gold-stamped but flakes faster than a headlamp - the old miners say that's proper, a crown shouldn't stay whole. On the disaster memorial day, a few lit ones always stand at the pithead.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_EasternStar: The "Eastern" is a factory east of Memphis and a typeface somebody picked out of a sample book. What is genuine is the inconsistency: the blend was never standardised, so no two cigarettes taste quite alike. Against boredom it beats the radio. Smoking one is like opening mail addressed to somebody else.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_Fable: Left behind by the first coauthor. Every one you burn is a draft, and the ash falls like deleted paragraphs. The last one will finish the story for it - the listener only needs to be present. On the bottom of the pack, one small line: all the stories are true, including this one.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_Frostline: A recipe from north of the frost line, cold straight to the crown of your head; the first drag opens your eyes wide. One in a panic and the heartbeat drops half a step - bottling-plant workers each keep one for month-end inventory. The company tried a mild version once. It was returned into discontinuation.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_GoldenCrane: Imported paper, local leaf, and the crane is real gold stamping - you can feel the raised edge. Handed out at weddings it reads as class, at funerals as respect; county folk call it the smoke that reaches both ends of life. The tin edition is discontinued. A family that still has one is planning to pass it down.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_GreenHollow: A politely cool smoke; the mint is grown down in the hollow itself, in batches too small to bother advertising. Folks raised there say it tastes like early morning at home: dew, the mint field, a little woodsmoke. The ones who moved to the city go quiet for a moment when they smell it.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_Highway60: The road smoke every gas station carries. They say that along Highway 60, every shelf is stocked exactly the same - third shelf, second slot from the left. Long-haul drivers use it as an odometer: one cigarette burns exactly one country song, one pack gets you from the county line to Louisville. The white line seems to stretch a little further.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_HollowCrown: The crown is hollow; the smoke is not - their 1966 slogan, never changed since. A sedative for patient people, steadier with every drag; most often found in the drawers of watchmakers and surgical nurses. The company never runs promotions. A cigarette in a hurry, they say, wouldn't deserve the name.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_KnoxStandard: Same red-and-white pack since 1958; even the typeface never changed. Every general store in the county keeps a few under the counter, close enough that the cashier can reach one without looking. Nobody praises them and nobody switches - in Knox County, loyalty isn't chosen, it's grown by habit.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_LastLight: In every pack one cigarette is placed upside down; the old rule says it is saved for the very last moment. The flipped one is not lent, not traded, not smoked early - bad luck otherwise, the one superstition every smoker in the county agrees on. Don't rush to throw the empty pack away, either. It remembers the time you made it through.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_Midnight100s: The extra length past a normal cigarette is reserved for the night shift. You'll find the dark-blue box at hospital back doors, in radio-station booths, in state-trooper cruisers. The longer the cigarette, the slower the dawn - so they say, and nobody laughs when they say it.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_NightWatch: The recipe is never written down; it has passed mouth to mouth between watchmen at shift change for thirty years. That night, they say, your eyes will not close - even blinking feels like waste. The debt comes due tomorrow. Watchman's rule: tonight's clarity, repaid with interest.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_OldMillReds: The mill closed in '81; the brand survived, its recipe bought whole by a city factory. Old hands have one quality test: smoke one at five in the morning, and the real thing keeps sleep outside the door. Better than an alarm clock, they say - you can silence an alarm.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_OldPhysician: A formula left by a doctor who lost his license and insisted to his last day that he'd been right. The way pain leaves the room is professionally unsettling, as if someone with a clipboard were showing it out patient by patient. Pharmacists privately call it the last page of the prescription pad - if you've turned to it, nothing earlier worked.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_Pinecrest: Half pine resin, half menthol; it smells like fresh-sawn timber. There is always a carton in a ranger's locker, and the one up in the fire tower holds a mountain alone with this and a radio. For every ten cartons sold the company donates binoculars to the forestry station. They never advertise that.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_Riverbend: The river on the pack was painted from the bend up north; the painter took the money and never signed. Light one on a bad day and the river does some of the flowing for you - that line is printed inside the pack, in small type you only see when it's empty. The county paper once ran a letter: I have never seen this river, but I believe it.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_SanCielo: Little cigars from the south, the tin printed with a sky burned through by sunset; inside the lid, one line of Spanish: what's the hurry. Smokers say stress scatters like afternoon clouds. Only two shops in the county stock it, and neither owner can explain the supply - it just arrives, on time, every month.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_SilentHunt: Something hunters roll out in the snow, softening the paper with body heat first. When the smoke spreads, even your heartbeat crouches down - they say a deer ten paces off can't hear you. It circulates only among hunting families. It has never seen the inside of a store.
ContextMenu_KCS_ST_SpiffosAlibi: Even a mascot needs a break. Behind every Spiffo's, they say, is a small patch of butts that belongs to him - two before the shift, two after. The smile is the job; the cigarette is his own. On the pack, Spiffo has taken the head off the suit. Nobody has seen the face. The pack only shows the back of his head.

ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_Ace: The ace of hearts sits a little off-centre; the factory never corrected it because nobody ever complained. Poolhall lighters live in shirt pockets and come out for other people's cigarettes more often than their own. Whoever carried this was generous with a flame and careful with money.
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_Black: Plain black enamel, no emblem, the cheapest finish they ever made - and it outsold every fancy one four to one. This is the lighter you buy once you have decided the lighter is not the point. Most of them died in washing machines.
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_Bourbon: A distillery gave these out at the 1989 county fair, one per adult, stamped with a barrel they had stopped using two years earlier. The bourbon was mediocre; the lighter was not, and it outlived the distillery by a decade.
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_Brass: Unplated brass, sold on the promise that it would take the colour of its owner. It does: dark at the hinge, bright along the seam a thumb crossed ten thousand times. Read it like a palm.
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_Camo: Woodland pattern, sold in sporting-goods aisles to men who hunted twice a year and carried the lighter every day. The pattern is useless at hiding a lighter and superb at telling a room what kind of weekend you would rather be having.
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_Chrome: Brushed chrome, made to hide fingerprints in its fine grain instead of showing them. Barbers liked it. Salesmen liked it. It catches the light without ever becoming a mirror -- a respectable finish for people who would rather not examine themselves before offering someone else a flame.
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_Derby: A horse mid-stride, engraved for the 1990 spring meeting. Half the county bet that year; a fifth of them are still telling the story. The engraving is worn smoothest across the horse's back, right where a thumb goes on the word "nearly".
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_Flag: Flag stripes over the whole case, a Bicentennial leftover that kept selling for seventeen years. Not out of ceremony: in a dark bar it is simply the easiest lighter on the table to find again.
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_Mermaid: A mermaid on verdigris enamel, from a seafood place four hundred miles from any sea. The owner had never been either. He just liked the sign, and the sign became the restaurant, and the restaurant put itself on two hundred lighters.
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_Miner: Crossed picks, issued at a retirement dinner eleven months before the seam closed. The gift said one thing and the timing said another. They were taken anyway; a lighter is a lighter, and a man still has to smoke.
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_Moon: Moon phases around the case, running the wrong way. The error surfaced after the first run; the corrected version sold worse, so the plates went back to being wrong. Collectors can tell at a glance. It has never mattered to anyone else.
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_RiverBelle: A paddle steamer that stopped running in 1974, printed on lighters until 1990 because the plates were already paid for. Two generations bought a boat they had never seen. That is one way a town keeps something.
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_RoadHawk: A hawk with its wings out, sold at truck stops beside the coffee. Long-haul drivers bought them two at a time: one for the cab, one for the man who would inevitably ask. This one has been in a cab. The enamel is faded on one side only, where the sun always was.
ContextMenu_KCS_ZDStory_Snake: Snakeskin texture pressed into the steel, which everybody in the county called ugly and which sold out every single year. Nobody has ever admitted to owning one on purpose. They all say it was a gift.

UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Blood_CleanRadius: Tile radius around the player checked during blood sweeps.

UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_CleanBlood: Manually removes floor and wall blood decals within your configured radius.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_CleanCorpse: Manually purges empty or junk zombie corpses in radius while strictly preserving weapons, bags, ammo, and keys.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_CleanDebris: Manually clears spent bullet casings, empty tins, broken glass, and twigs from the ground.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Combat_BurstSmoother: Buffers simultaneous multi-kill impact bursts across 2-3 frames to eliminate combat freezing during shotgun blasts & katana multi-hits.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Corpse_AutoClean: Periodically sweeps away aged zombie corpses in your local zone to reduce CPU entity tracking.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Corpse_CleanAshAndSke: Immediately sweeps away skeletonized dead bodies and burnt ash piles to keep streets clean.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Corpse_CleanEmptyOnly: Only removes corpses whose inventory is completely empty, ensuring 100%% of zombie loot is preserved.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Corpse_CleanJunkOnly: Cleans corpses that only carry worn clothes while strictly saving weapons, ammo, bags, keys, and watches.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Corpse_CleanRadius: Tile radius around the player checked during corpse sweeps.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Corpse_CullShadows: Disables dynamic 3D shadow stencils on dead corpses to save draw calls in horde battles.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Corpse_IntervalHours: In-game hours between automated zombie corpse sweeps.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Corpse_MinAgeHours: Minimum hours a corpse must have been dead before it is eligible for cleanup.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Corpse_MuteFlies: Silences annoying buzzing fly audio emitters on dead zombie bodies.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Debris_AutoClean: Periodically scans and cleans clutter items dropped in the world based on the item filters below.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Debris_CleanBrokenGla: Cleans dangerous broken window glass shards on the floor to prevent tire punctures and lacerations.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Debris_CleanCasings: Cleans up spent bullet shells and empty ammunition casings on the floor (supports vanilla and gun mods).
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Debris_CleanRadius: Distance in tiles around the player to search for ground debris.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Debris_CleanRottenFoo: Purges completely rotten expired food items left dropped on the ground to reduce save bloat.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Debris_CleanTrash: Removes discarded empty food cans, empty soda bottles, candy wrappers, and cigarette butts.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Debris_CleanTwigsAndW: Removes naturally spawned foraging twigs, tree branches, and stones from roadways and paved areas (Logs and log stacks are permanently protected).
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Debris_IntervalHours: In-game hours between ground clutter and trash cleanup sweeps.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_FBORender_CheapOcclus: Optimizes cutaway wall and multi-story occlusion calculations for smooth interior frame rates.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Fire_MaxEmitters: Caps overlapping burning zombie scream sound loops.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Fire_ThrottleParticle: Caps maximum active fire particles to 50 and vortices to 2 during large building and zombie fires.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_GC_PurgeThresholdMB: Memory usage cutoff threshold required before Smart Idle Garbage Collection triggers a background sweep.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_GC_SmartIdleGC: Runs gentle memory sweeps only when you are safely sleeping, reading, or resting indoors with zero nearby zombies.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_GFX_BuildingInteriorC: Culls hidden lower floors and unviewable exterior ground tiles when inside multi-story buildings and skyscrapers. Automatically restores near windows & balconies.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_GFX_CustomShaders: Enables the mod's optimized screen-space puddle wave shaders and multi-pass wall shaders. Uncheck to bypass all custom shaders and use high-speed 2D flat tiles/puddles (recommended for Potato mode or if experiencing GPU driver glitches).
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_GFX_DynamicReflection: Disabling eliminates secondary reflection passes on roads and puddles, curing Build 42 driving and rain stutter.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_GFX_DynamicZoomLOD: Dynamically scales sub-pixel ground debris and skeleton blending when zoomed out to 150-250%% to eliminate zoom-out frame lag.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_GFX_EnforceTextureCom: Forces texture compression in options.ini, cutting VRAM usage in half and stopping texture loading hitching.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_GFX_ForestCanopyCull: Culls wind sway vertex math on fully enclosed deep interior trees, keeping 100%% of outer forest canopy silhouette intact.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_GFX_ModelLighting: Uncheck in Potato Mode to shade character/zombie meshes with ambient room light rather than per-vertex dynamic point lights.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Horde_AccelerateAnimF: Transitions distant zombies into stepped LOD animation poses sooner, eliminating frame drops when large swarms approach.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Horde_AudioConcurrenc: Limits simultaneous overlapping zombie groan and footstep audio emitters to the nearest 16 zombies to stop audio crackling and FMOD CPU lag.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Horde_CullDistantAtta: Suppresses tiny non-essential 3D cosmetic accessories on distant zombies in large 30+ swarms.

UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Horde_OffscreenAnimDe: Skips skeletal mesh bone and animation math for zombies outside your camera view.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Horde_StaggeredAITick: Staggers zombie A* navigation recalculations across a 4-phase round-robin cycle to drop swarm AI CPU load by 75%%.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Horde_ThrottleStaticA: Reduces skeletal animation update frequency for idle, sleeping, or standing characters to 15 FPS to save massive CPU cycles.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Hotkey: Hotkey used to toggle the Project Zomboid Optimiser Control Center (Default: F10)
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_JVM_AsyncModelCompile: Compiles character clothing, armor, and vehicle 3D textures across background CPU threads to eliminate equipment swap frame drops.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_JVM_DeepChunkCache: Keeps recently streamed road and town chunks cached in 8GB+ RAM to completely eliminate disk read stutters when turning around or retracing paths.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_JVM_FMODSpatialCullin: Bypasses heavy wall-occlusion and low-pass DSP calculations for sounds beyond 35 tiles or below hearing threshold. Lowers audio thread CPU load during 100+ zombie combat.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_JVM_GLStateOptimizer: Filters redundant shader uniform uploads (lighting, fog, ambient color) and 3D clothing bone matrices before sending them to the GPU driver. Boosts FPS in dense cities.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_JVM_HordeHibernation: Hibernates distant off-screen zombie pathfinding and animation state in RAM buffers to save massive CPU cycles in mega-horde territory.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_JVM_KahluaGCPacer: Smoothly collects Lua garbage in 50-step increments every frame to prevent dead mod tables from accumulating and triggering 20-30ms stutter spikes during vehicle travel.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_JVM_PowerShield: Locks Windows/Linux multimedia high-performance thread scheduling and prioritizes Performance Cores (P-Cores) over Efficiency Cores on Intel 12th-15th Gen and AMD X3D CPUs.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_JVM_PurgeRAM: Immediately triggers a native JVM and Kahlua memory collection cycle to release unreferenced heap memory.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_JVM_StreamBufferBoost: Enables 128KB page-aligned direct NIO memory stream buffers and ChunkBufferPool for stutter-free road chunk loading at 70+ mph.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_JVM_ZeroStutterGC: Eliminates in-game stop-the-world Lua garbage collection pauses during combat and driving by offloading memory management to background G1GC worker threads.
UI_MPOptim_Tooltip_Lighting_FPS: Controls the target update framerate for dynamic lighting propagation. Lower values (15-30 FPS) save huge CPU cycles.
